overall_intent: Grounded photographic LitRPG craft transaction where readable item rules, maker progression and payment form one visible connected scene.

required_constraints: The fantasy interaction remains a purchase affected by item appraisal.
Use reference appearance only for the main fictional woman; retain literal reference scope.
Physical item and its readable item state must visibly connect in one photograph.
preserved_choices: Main human subject and everyday fantasy artisan/customer interaction.

review.author: Codex
review.rationale: The slot develops the independent frozen craft transaction within open staging; it does not create a new requester definition or lock.

narrative_core.reason: The transaction needs a visible cause and decision rather than a decorative game interface.
narrative_core.expressive_goal: A humble crafted object changes perceived worth when explicit item rules are appraised.
observable_targets: Maker, customer and one crafted item in a shared working space.
An item appraisal visibly affecting payment or a purchase decision.
owner_relations: Maker presents her completed work to a buyer.
The appraisal belongs to the same physical item between them.
open_scope: Local gestures, price/payment staging, environmental craft context, timing within appraisal.
narrative_core.role_focus: An everyday fantasy artisan and buyer evaluate a newly crafted item; explicit item properties alter the customer purchase decision and make the work consequential.
narrative_core.scene_context: A glassblower-appraiser at a cold workshop counter steadies a completed blue lantern vial; a marsh surveyor begins payment after learning its useful fog-related property.

grounds.quote: A completed lantern vial is appraised and the customer places payment; specifics are authorial.

visible_text.reason: Quantified item state and artisan progression must read as world rules with visible owners.
visible_text.expressive_goal: Spare legible RPG information clarifies why this item and its maker matter.
observable_targets: A readable item card connected to its physical item.
A smaller job or crafting progress badge tied to the artisan.
owner_relations: Item card endpoint lands on the lantern vial.
Craft progression badge visibly belongs to the maker rather than the buyer.
open_scope: Card placement, minimal wording, visual leader line, information hierarchy.
visible_text.role_focus: Readable in-world item appraisal values with a visible connector to their actual object, plus secondary crafting skill progression visibly assigned to the artisan.
visible_text.scene_context: A medium landscape workshop transaction keeps two faces, hands, vial and full short appraisal text visible; the card must explain an actual purchase rather than decorate the frame.

grounds.quote: Independently chosen glassblower appraisal transaction realizes the contextual LitRPG topic: visible rule-governed item state affects an everyday fantasy profession and a purchase. The reference guides face and hair only. The viewer should feel a modest crafted object acquire surprising value through a legible item-to-system-to-payment chain. Saved creativity=1 keeps later variations local; sensual=1 supports the maker through soft light, open-neck linen and quietly confident presence; fetish=0, surreal=0 retain only requested fantasy. Glassblower, vial, stat wording, customer, furnace and all staging are agent choices, not requester-owned locks. Simultaneous endpoints require a landscape medium table view with a sparse card and clear hands.
